applicable_when: The kernel uses 255 registers/thread — the hardware maximum — which limits the SM to only 2 active blocks (8 warps total, 2 per scheduler). With only 1.99 active warps/scheduler and 0.73 eligible warps/scheduler, 58% of cycles have no instruction to issue. The root cause is the large BLOCK_M=128 x BLOCK_N=128 accumulator tile (128x128 fp32 = 16384 values) combined with BLOCK_K=32 and no software pipelining (num_stages=1 implied). Reducing tile sizes (e.g., BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=64) shrinks the accumulator to 4096 values, freeing registers for more concurrent warps. Adding num_stages=3 enables software pipelining to hide memory latency. Wrapping in @triton.autotune lets the H200 runtime select the optimal config from a curated set.
